summary.text: A 45-year-old female with good performance status and an unremarkable family history presented in February 2019 with lower abdominal pain and dysuria for 5 months after failed conservative measures. Ultrasound, cystoscopy and a transurethral resection biopsy showed a left lateral bladder wall submucosal growth with spindle cell tumor, SMA positive and GATA3 and cytokeratin negative, and leiomyosarcoma was diagnosed.

Whole body FDG PET-CECT showed a 4.9 × 5.3 × 4.6 cm necrotic bladder mass, pelvic and paraaortic nodes and a doubtful right adrenal nodule. With stage IV disease she received palliative VAC/IE chemotherapy; after 3 cycles she had persistent symptoms and local progression, and received palliative pelvic radiotherapy of 30 Gy in 10 fractions and six cycles of second-line gemcitabine plus docetaxel.

She had recurrent hematuria, and imaging suggested progressive bladder growth with unchanged nodal disease; after multidisciplinary discussion she was advised surgery in view of good performance status and persistent symptoms. Radical cystectomy and hysterectomy specimens showed pleomorphic leiomyosarcoma with perivesical fat invasion and a close margin, and the nodes showed granulomas. The initial nodal metastatic diagnosis was revised and adjuvant radiotherapy of 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions was delivered.

Two months after radiotherapy she presented with projectile vomiting, constipation and upper gastrointestinal bleed. Emergency laparotomy found an obstructing 5 × 4 cm growth at the ileal anastomotic site, resected, and histology suggested metastatic leiomyosarcoma. Within 6 weeks of that surgery a left lumbar swelling, first thought an abscess, was proven metastatic on cytology, and PET-CECT showed paraaortic nodes and serosal deposits.

Metronomic chemotherapy was advised because of low performance status but could not be started because of declining oral intake. She died 2 months after the last PET imaging, with an overall survival of 1.7 years since diagnosis.

caption_evidence.quote:
Fig. 2
A Radical cystectomy specimen showing urinary bladder with a large necrotic and fungating growth arising from left lateral wall with serosal involvement. The resected hysterectomy specimen shows a leiomyoma. B Photomicrograph showing tumor with overlying urothelial epithelium. Eosinophilic spindle shaped tumor cells are arranged in storiform pattern and interlacing fascicles (H&E, × 40). C Tumor is infiltrating bladder muscle (H&E, × 40). D Immunohistochemistry (IHC) shows expression of smooth muscle actin (SMA) in the tumor cells (SMA immunostain, × 200). E Sections from intestinal mass showed an invasive well-demarcated tumor arising from muscularis mucosae and extending transmurally to reach the serosa. Photomicrograph shows spindle cell tumor arranged in short and long fascicles (H&E, × 40). F High magnification showing increased mitotic activity in the spindle shaped tumor cells (H&E, × 400). G On IHC, the tumor cells were negative for CD34, and H negative for DOG1
